chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying, and he was asked about marriage in the month of Shawwal, so he said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) married Aisha in Shawwal.' And he said: 'It was only disliked in Shawwal by the people of the early times, and that is because the plague used to affect them among the virgins and the slave girls, so they disliked it for that reason, not for any other reason.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الزَّمَنِ الْأَوَّل: The people of the early times
key_terms.شَوَّال: Shawwal (the 10th month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: Why was marriage in Shawwal disliked in early Islamic times?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that marriage in Shawwal is permissible, citing the Prophet’s marriage to Aisha in this month. The dislike for Shawwal marriage was a cultural practice of early Muslims due to outbreaks of plague affecting virgins and slave girls, not a religious prohibition.
